video_title: OpenAI’s Head of ChatGPT: We’re entering a new era of AI (again) | Tibo Sottiaux
gist: Tibo Sottiaux (OpenAI, ChatGPT/Codex) discusses the DevDay launches: an always-on personal agent, the planned merge of Codex and ChatGPT, an open plugin ecosystem with revenue share, his view that most internet actions will come from agents, safety spend, and OpenAI culture and hiring. Note the transcript is auto-generated, so product and model names are garbled.

insights.claim: Sottiaux says the majority of actions on the internet will be taken by agents, and he lists this as the first of three things he believes are not yet priced in.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Agent-driven demand shifts where product traffic, API load and value capture sit; incumbents built only for human UIs are exposed.
insights.quote: The majority of actions on the internet will be taken by agents.

insights.claim: Products must be built for agent-scale load. Notion's MCP, built with OpenAI's help, exposed it to many agents and brought a ton of traffic, which strained the system and forced them to work out the economics.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Agent access creates a real cost-to-serve problem; pricing and rate-limit design for agent traffic becomes a competitive variable.
insights.quote: if you want your product to be successful for agents, you know, it's like you have to build you know, for a certain level of scale.

insights.claim: There is a tension for product builders over whether to build an agent-facing interface. Sottiaux calls it inevitable that most usage will come from agents, though it can be held back for a while.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Companies that delay agent interfaces to protect human-facing economics risk losing distribution to those that open up.

insights.claim: Building delightful new experiences for humans, especially ones that benefit from older modalities, is under-invested, even as agents take over most actions.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: A possible white space: human-facing experiences that differentiate while agents handle commodity tasks.

insights.claim: Sottiaux says builders are under-ambitious. If they imagined all of this being roughly 10x better in a year, they would build differently.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Product roadmaps based on today's capability will be obsolete quickly; the capability curve is the planning input.
insights.quote: if you were just like pushing yourself and just really imagining like all of this being roughly 10 times better than it is today, you know, like in a year.

insights.claim: Models will keep getting cheaper and faster at rates he calls incredible, and all modalities will be integrated seamlessly. These are the other two items on his not-priced-in list.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Falling cost and latency, plus multimodal integration, widen the set of use cases that become economic.
insights.quote: Models are going to become more cheaper and faster at rates that are quite incredible.

insights.claim: OpenAI launched a persistent assistant (called 'dots' in the auto-transcript) as a smart agent that works 24/7, knows your goals and preferences, learns from feedback, and is reachable through any client or screen. Sottiaux frames it as the direction of the whole product line.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: The competitive frame moves from chat apps to a persistent agent layer; the switching cost is accumulated memory and preferences.
insights.quote: you have an incredibly smart agent that works 24/7, understands your goals, understands your preferences, learns from feedback.

insights.claim: He rejects hand-configured loops as the long-term model. People got excited about tuning loops, but over time users want a system that learns what they want to achieve.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Orchestration and loop-tuning tooling is likely a transitional layer that gets absorbed into the model and agent.
insights.quote: having to set up and fiddle with your loops and, you know, figuring that out is something that, you know, maybe people got excited about, but I don't think this is the way that it's going to work.

insights.claim: His personal agent-team size oscillates. He builds larger teams of agents while pushing the frontier. When a model breakthrough arrives, a bigger single agent can do it all with memory, so he shrinks the team, then expands again.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Multi-agent scaffolding compensates for model limits and is repeatedly collapsed as models improve, which is a risk for agent-orchestration startups.
insights.quote: I find myself like, you know, building larger and larger teams of agents. And then, when we have the next breakthrough with models

insights.claim: The assistant's architecture separates the harness from the device. The harness does not run on the user's machine, the agent has its own computer, and it can connect to many devices at once, which he likens to an octopus. Specialist instances run with extra guardrails and monitoring on their own hardware, some on Mac minis.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Cloud-resident agents controlling many endpoints is the design that differs from local-first agent tools.
insights.quote: the harness does not run on the machine.

insights.claim: Users get one primary assistant at launch, with the ability to add more to form a virtual team with specific roles coming soon. Sottiaux runs one just for Twitter monitoring.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Multi-agent-per-user is a likely seat/usage expansion lever for monetization.

insights.claim: The assistant proactively flagged a ChatGPT production outage five minutes before the DevDay live demo by connecting the live demo to the production system. It offered to fix it, and Sottiaux judged it not yet capable of that.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Shows that proactive context-linking is working, while autonomous remediation of production systems remains beyond current reliability.
insights.quote: I don't think you're there yet, you know, little dot but you know, thank you for trying

insights.claim: OpenAI says the long-horizon persistent task research and memory systems took more than two years of work. The assistant launch combines that with the Codex harness and 24/7 running, and ships with its safest, most aligned model ('Astra' in the transcript).
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: The product is the product of compounding research in memory and long-horizon tasks, which is a moat versus fast followers of open-source agent projects.

insights.claim: OpenAI will merge chat and the 'work' toggle, reducing complexity, and eventually ship all of the assistant's capabilities into ChatGPT to lift the floor for its roughly 1.2 billion users.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Agentic capability gets distributed through the largest consumer base, a distribution advantage over agent-native startups.
insights.quote: we're going to merge

insights.claim: Model pickers, reasoning-effort settings and multi-agent versus ultra choices are a pain point. The assistant has no model picker and only needs channels configured, and Sottiaux wants the app to nearly disappear into simplicity.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Configuration burden is an adoption barrier; expect auto-routing of models and effort to become the norm.
insights.quote: you kind of need a PhD in model pickers.

insights.claim: Voice, multimodal input and shared whiteboard-style collaborative surfaces between humans and agents are expected to transcend conversations and today's clients. Sottiaux says the current experience still feels clunky until it isn't.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Interface competition moves beyond chat windows to ambient and multimodal surfaces.
insights.quote: it still feels like a bit clunky and I think it will feel clunky until it isn't.

insights.claim: Sottiaux names the ecosystem as the sleeper hit of the launches: Sign in with ChatGPT with 16 partners, plugin extensions and discovery, and access to roughly 1.2 billion users. It began informally with the creators of Pi and OpenCode, who used ChatGPT subscription auth on trust.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: OpenAI is turning subscription usage into a platform others build on, which makes ChatGPT a distribution channel and subsidizes third-party agents.
insights.quote: the sleeper hit is ecosystem.

insights.claim: OpenAI will share revenue with popular plugins and with products using sign-in with ChatGPT, tied to subscriber usage consumed inside them. This was not announced in the keynote.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: A rev-share app-store model for agents: partners like Notion or Figma could monetize from ChatGPT subscribers, and economics are still unspecified.
insights.quote: we will have like some shared economics with them

insights.claim: Plugin discovery is merit-based. OpenAI looks at retention and quality and recommends plugins in conversations, and poor ones stop being recommended. This is not an AEO-style keyword game.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Distribution depends on sustained usage metrics, favoring products that deliver real utility over marketing.
insights.quote: we look at retention uh numbers

insights.claim: Sottiaux defines pacing the frontier as investing ahead in alignment, security and guardrails. OpenAI is spending growing compute on secondary monitoring agents that watch the primary agent for risky actions and prompt injection, and he says the majority of its API-stack investment is not going into the safety stack.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Safety monitoring is becoming a material compute cost line for agent products, and a source of demand for secure inference.
insights.quote: We are spending more and more compute on sort of like secondary monitoring.

insights.claim: OpenAI says it has not released the next capability step beyond 'Astra'. It released a near-Astra-intelligence model that is much more efficient, and a previous Astra version was withheld, which he is proud of. He ties this to incentives: serving 1.2 billion people means they cannot gamble.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Signals a staggered release posture where efficiency is shipped first and frontier capability is held back for safety.
insights.quote: we don't gamble there.

insights.claim: He expected today's model capability level (Astra-class) in a year or two and had to revise his priors. He also underestimated how much he would use voice and dictation, and how much younger generations would lead adoption.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Insider timelines for capability arrived earlier than expected, and users move to voice quickly once latency is good.

insights.claim: A breakthrough in ultra-fast inference restored flow state for Sottiaux, letting him run fewer agents in parallel. A 6-month-old version of ultrafast is coming soon at roughly the same cost as Astra, and voice control with that speed brings back a creative flow.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Latency is a distinct product axis from intelligence, and fast models change the interaction pattern toward less parallelism.
insights.quote: I'm able to be in the flow again

themes.theme: Talent, culture and the future of work

insights.claim: Skills trending down are fast typing; trending up are taste, thinking about the user and knowing what good looks like. Roles blur, which suits product-minded generalists. OpenAI has more than 120 ex-founders (transcribed as XYC), and Sottiaux says new grads who embrace AI and learn quickly have an advantage.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Hiring premium shifts from execution skills to judgment and product sense; ex-founders cluster at AI labs.
insights.quote: skill that is trending down is typing fast.

insights.claim: Sottiaux says he is not hand-writing code anymore and that Codex writes most of his analysis code. He claims we may not have coders anymore but we have more builders than ever, and that humans will still prefer to hear from other humans.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: A senior insider describes coding as already largely delegated, and the human role as taste and will.
insights.quote: we may not have coders anymore, but we have more builders than ever.

insights.claim: OpenAI's internal culture is bottoms-up. The decisions API started as four people hacking on a weekend, using constrained sampling on a strong model ('Luna') as a new shape of the Responses API. A quality bar holds back launches, and some items were pulled from DevDay.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Shipping velocity comes from autonomy plus gatekeeping at the end, not top-down roadmaps.

insights.claim: Agent-heavy work risks fatigue, solitude and pressure to do more. Sottiaux says the promise of AI is reduced noise and focus rather than one more prompt per second, with possibly fewer meetings and better-rested people.
insights.speaker: Tibo Sottiaux
insights.so_what: Productivity gains may be competed away into more output expectations; products that reduce attention load are a stated design goal.
insights.quote: it's not you know, just one more prompt you know, per second.
